desc.k17447: Lp(a) is a lipoprotein linked to atherosclerosis and thrombosis, used to assess cardiovascular risk. It is particularly relevant when there is a family history of early cardiovascular disease, or disease or a heart attack that is not well explained by traditional risk factors.
desc.k17414: Measures lithium during treatment to check whether exposure to the medicine is appropriate and to assess toxicity. Interpretation takes into account the dose, kidney function, hydration, salt in the diet and other medicines, because the margin between a therapeutic and a toxic effect is narrow.
desc.k17698: Looks for lupus anticoagulant, antibodies linked to the risk of thrombosis and to antiphospholipid syndrome. It is used after thromboses, a prolonged partial thromboplastin time or recurrent miscarriages; despite its name, it is not used to diagnose or monitor systemic lupus erythematosus.
desc.k17415: Measures magnesium to assess electrolyte disorders that can cause arrhythmia, weakness or irritability. It is also used when potassium or calcium levels are abnormal and to monitor magnesium sulphate therapy, especially in the context of pre-eclampsia.
desc.k54260: The profile tracks the daily rhythm of melatonin with three saliva measurements. It is used to look into sleep disorders and sleep–wake rhythm disorders, comparing how the hormone is distributed over the day and night with the individual's clinical situation.
desc.k18234: Measures mercury in serum when poisoning or significant exposure is suspected. Possible sources include industrial and environmental sources, occupational exposure and foods such as large predatory fish; the result is interpreted by the doctor in relation to the exposure history and symptoms.
desc.k18235: Measures mercury in a single urine sample, especially to assess and monitor occupational exposure to inorganic forms. The description links mercury build-up with kidney damage and distinguishes this use from blood testing, which assesses exposure to organic forms through fish.
desc.k55321: Measures oestrogens, their hydroxylated and methylated metabolites and their ratios in urine to describe how oestrogen is metabolised.
desc.k46471: The profile combines urine and blood markers to assess metabolism and nutritional needs. It analyses organic acids, amino acids, fatty acids, oxidative stress, nutrient and toxic elements and neurotransmitter metabolites, providing additional information in fatigue, malabsorption and metabolic or nutritional disorders.
desc.k85075: Metabolomix+ with genetics combines the metabolic and nutritional profile with selected genetic variants. The tests examine energy metabolism, amino acids, fats, oxidative stress and nutrient and toxic elements, while the genetic part adds information on predispositions related to methylation, inflammation and metabolism.
desc.k38638: Measures metanephrine, normetanephrine and 3-methoxytyramine in plasma to investigate catecholamine-producing tumours. It is used when persistent or episodic high blood pressure is accompanied by headaches, palpitations and sweating, helping to assess for phaeochromocytoma, paraganglioma or other neuroendocrine tumours.
desc.k18215: The panel measures catecholamine metabolites in 24-hour urine to investigate phaeochromocytoma, paraganglioma and other neuroendocrine tumours. It may be requested when high blood pressure is accompanied by episodes of palpitations, headache, sweating, pallor or tremor.
desc.k17682: Methylmercury is an organic form of mercury that can build up in the body, mainly through fish and seafood. Measuring it in the blood is used to assess exposure to this form, especially in people who eat a lot of these foods, taking into account the risk of neurological damage.
desc.k17622: Measures the percentage of methaemoglobin, an oxidised form of haemoglobin that does not carry oxygen normally. It helps diagnose and monitor inherited or acquired methaemoglobinaemia, especially when there is cyanosis or hypoxia after exposure to medicines, chemicals or oxidising substances.
desc.k18302: Looks for Y chromosome microdeletions, including in the AZF regions, when investigating azoospermia or oligospermia. The result can help clarify the genetic cause of male infertility, assess options for assisted reproduction and inform counselling about passing the change on to male offspring.
desc.k29429: Measures essential minerals and toxic metals in red blood cells to assess mineral status and longer-term exposure. It is suggested for suspected nutritional deficiencies, absorption disorders, chronic symptoms or occupational and environmental exposure to metals; interpretation depends on the clinical history.
desc.k17520: Myoglobin is released quickly into the blood after damage to heart or skeletal muscle. The measurement is used as an early marker of muscle damage and, together with other cardiac markers, in investigating a heart attack or a repeat heart attack; a rise is not specific to the heart alone.
desc.k17310: Measures specific IgE to chicken meat to investigate a suspected allergic reaction. A positive result indicates sensitisation and is assessed together with symptoms after eating chicken; many sensitised people have no symptoms, while a negative result does not completely rule out allergy.
desc.k17305: The test measures specific IgE to honey, allergen f247, to help investigate allergic or anaphylactic reactions. A positive result may indicate sensitisation only, without clinical allergy, while a negative result does not completely rule out allergy; the result is assessed by an allergist together with the symptoms.
desc.k49039: IGRA measures the cellular immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens. It is used to screen for latent infection after contact, before biological or immunosuppressive therapy and in at-risk groups; interpretation requires correlation with other tuberculosis tests.
desc.k18303: Detects DNA of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex directly in the clinical sample to help diagnose pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis quickly. The result is assessed together with the clinical picture, microscopy and culture; a negative result does not completely rule out infection, and the test is not used to monitor whether treatment is working.
desc.k17260: The mx1 mix measures specific IgE to the four listed moulds and is used to investigate the cause of allergic reactions or anaphylaxis. The test supports the assessment of mould allergy or sensitisation when matched with symptoms and the history of contact.
desc.k17422: Sodium is an electrolyte important for fluid balance, acid–base status and nerve and muscle function. The measurement is used in routine check-ups and in investigating or monitoring dehydration, fluid retention, blood pressure disorders and diseases that disturb these balances.
desc.k17423: Measures sodium excreted in urine collected over 24 hours. It helps investigate disorders of water and sodium balance, oedema and blood pressure, and assess kidney function in relation to sodium intake and losses.
desc.k51133: Measures nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B3 involved in many reactions of energy metabolism and cell maintenance. Testing may help when niacin deficiency is suspected, especially pellagra with signs such as dermatitis, diarrhoea and neurological changes.
desc.k18184: Measures neuron-specific enolase to help assess small cell lung cancer and monitor NSE-secreting tumours. It is used to follow treatment response or recurrence in neuroblastoma, carcinoids and pancreatic endocrine tumours, always together with clinical and diagnostic findings.
desc.k17909: The test measures NT-proBNP, the inactive fragment released together with BNP, which reflects strain on the heart chambers. It is used as an aid in diagnosing congestive heart failure and in monitoring its course or response to treatment.
desc.k20035: NutrEval combines blood and urine biomarkers for a functional assessment of nutritional and metabolic status. The report looks at possible needs for vitamins, minerals, antioxidants and fatty acids, as well as markers of energy metabolism, digestion, oxidative stress and exposure to metals.
desc.k21298: The nutrigenetic test analyses five variants in four genes linked to energy balance and the metabolism of fats and sugars. According to the description, it aims to support advice on nutrition, weight control and physical activity based on the individual's genetic profile.
desc.k17448: Measures daily oxalate excretion to assess the risk of kidney stones coming back and to monitor hyperoxaluria. The value can be affected by inherited disorders, fat malabsorption or a high intake of oxalates and vitamin C.
desc.k17514: Oxytocin is a hormone involved in uterine contractions, milk let-down and other reproductive processes. The source presents its measurement as part of the assessment of hormonal disorders, infertility, postpartum problems and the monitoring of certain reproductive procedures.
desc.k17658: Organix/MAP measures more than 40 organic metabolites in urine for a functional assessment of metabolic pathways and nutritional needs. The report includes markers of cellular energy, vitamins, digestion, neurotransmitters, oxalates and toxin exposure; it does not diagnose inborn genetic disorders of metabolism.
desc.k18172: Osteocalcin is a marker of bone turnover and is used with other markers to monitor treatment of metabolic bone diseases. It helps assess the effect of antiresorptive therapy but does not establish a diagnosis of osteoporosis; kidney function can affect the result.
desc.k17772: The test looks for p-ANCA/anti-MPO autoantibodies as an aid in diagnosing and monitoring certain autoimmune diseases, especially systemic vasculitis. It is requested when clinical signs raise suspicion of these disorders, and the result is assessed together with other findings.
desc.k21211: This comprehensive panel examines 54 genes linked to more than 30 types of cancer in several organs to assess inherited predisposition. Identifying a pathogenic variant can help with follow-up and family assessment; a negative result does not rule out cancer from other causes or from factors not yet known.
desc.k55609: The panel combines measurement of methylation metabolites in blood with genetic analysis from a cheek swab, to examine how this cycle is working and any inherited predispositions. The laboratory offers it for the functional assessment of fatigue and metabolic or neurological disorders, and to guide individualised recommendations based on the findings.
desc.k55606: The panel measures metabolites in blood to examine how methylation is working biochemically, without genetic analysis. Interpretation is based on the relationships between several metabolites.
desc.k80608: The panel combines blood tests with a urine test to assess fever, fatigue or suspected infection. It helps look at inflammation, blood cells, glucose, liver and kidney function, electrolytes and possible signs of a urinary tract infection.
desc.k80611: The panel helps with the initial assessment of fever, fatigue and suspected infection. It includes a full blood count, CRP, glucose, ALT, AST, urea, creatinine and the electrolytes sodium, potassium and chloride, to look at inflammation, metabolism, liver and kidney function and fluid balance.
desc.k34960: This hereditary panel examines 22 genes linked to Fanconi anaemia, a group of disorders with genomic instability, malformations and early bone marrow failure. The test helps with the genetic assessment of this condition and the associated predisposition to leukaemia or solid tumours.
desc.k34964: A seven-gene panel for inherited predispositions that may show up as tumours in several organs and tissues. It supports the assessment of syndromes such as Li-Fraumeni, PTEN predisposition, DICER1 and Peutz-Jeghers, in relation to the personal and family history of cancer.
desc.k34958: This genetic panel investigates inherited predispositions to endocrine tumours, including multiple endocrine neoplasia, paraganglioma–phaeochromocytoma syndromes and CDC73-related disorders. It analyses 14 genes and can help assess patients or families with relevant signs and history.
desc.k21224: The panel analyses 20 genes linked to inherited predisposition to gastrointestinal tumours. It notably covers hereditary diffuse gastric cancer and juvenile polyposis, helping to assess family risk and plan appropriate clinical follow-up.
desc.k34961: This genetic panel looks for inherited changes linked to a predisposition to breast and ovarian cancer. It is described especially for families with frequent cases or diagnoses before the age of 50 and can help plan follow-up for people at risk.
desc.k21209: Analyses 19 genes for inherited predisposition to breast and ovarian cancer, including BRCA1/BRCA2 and other risk genes. It is recommended when these cancers occur repeatedly in a family or were diagnosed at a young age, to support genetic assessment and individual follow-up.
desc.k34965: The panel analyses 14 genes linked to inherited predisposition to skin cancers, including melanoma. It helps assess syndromes such as BAP1 tumour predisposition and familial melanoma with multiple atypical naevi, taking into account personal and family history.
desc.k34962: This genetic panel for pancreatic cancer analyses 15 genes linked to inherited predisposition to this disease and related syndromes. Choosing and interpreting the test requires the family history and genetic counselling, as some cases have a hereditary component.
desc.k34955: The panel examines variants in 11 genes linked to inherited predisposition to prostate cancer and other tumour syndromes. It aims at genetic risk assessment and at choosing appropriate testing, taking into account the personal and family history of cancer.
desc.k34963: This panel analyses 14 genes linked to inherited tumour syndromes that can affect the brain or other parts of the central nervous system. It is used to assess genetic predisposition, including syndromes such as neurofibromatosis and Von Hippel–Lindau, in the context of personal and family history.
desc.k34959: This genetic panel examines 11 genes linked to an inherited predisposition to kidney cancer. The description includes syndromes such as hereditary leiomyomatosis, Birt–Hogg–Dubé and familial papillary carcinoma, to help assess patients and their relatives.
desc.k34957: The result is used together with personal/family history and genetic counselling to help assess risk and plan follow-up.
desc.k34956: This basic panel analyses 16 genes linked to inherited colorectal cancer syndromes. The result helps assess familial predisposition and plan follow-up for people at risk, and is interpreted alongside the personal and family history of cancer.
desc.k21272: Liquid-based cervical cytology to detect cell changes that may be precancerous or cancerous. It can also show inflammation or infection; results are reported using the Bethesda system with reference to the Papanicolaou classification, and suspicious findings may need further assessment.
desc.k21271: Combines liquid-based cervical cytology with HPV typing from the same sample to assess cell changes and the risk of precancerous lesions. The examination may also reveal inflammation or infections; results and repeat testing are decided together with the gynaecologist.
desc.k21371: The Pap test examines cells from the cervix for precancerous changes or changes suspicious for cancer, with the aim of early detection. It is a screening test; abnormal findings may need follow-up, colposcopy or biopsy, and the result is interpreted by the doctor according to the patient's condition.
desc.k17941: Measures the placental protein PAPP-A as part of combined first-trimester screening, together with free beta hCG, ultrasound and maternal factors. It helps assess the risk of chromosomal abnormalities and disorders of placental development; a single value does not make a diagnosis.
desc.k17290: Quantitatively measures specific IgE to paracetamol to help investigate a previous allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result without symptoms indicates sensitisation, while a negative result does not rule out allergy; diagnosis requires assessment by an allergist or immunologist.
desc.k51567: Peptiduria examines urinary peptides linked to incomplete digestion of gluten and casein, as well as the metabolite IAG. The laboratory uses it as part of a functional assessment of gastrointestinal or neurodevelopmental complaints, but stresses that the test does not diagnose autism or the other conditions mentioned.
desc.k17566: This urine panel aims to detect the groups of drugs and medicines included in the panel.
desc.k17565: This urine panel covers five groups of substances: amphetamine, cocaine, morphine, cannabinoids and MDMA.
desc.k76915: CAR measures the change in salivary cortisol immediately after waking, as information on the hormonal rhythm and the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis.
desc.k17357: This test measures specific IgE to house dust h1 and helps identify the trigger after an allergic reaction or anaphylactic episode. The result is used to assess allergy or sensitisation, together with symptoms and exposure history.
desc.k18236: Lead measurement helps assess exposure and investigate acute or chronic poisoning, including occupational exposure. Urine measurement looks at elimination and can be used during follow-up after treatment or when exposure continues, together with the clinical picture.
desc.k17355: This test measures specific IgE to the wp5 pollen mix to help identify the trigger after an allergic reaction or anaphylactic episode. It supports the assessment of allergy or sensitisation to the listed plants, in relation to symptoms and clinical history.
desc.k17564: The gx1 mix measures specific IgE to the pollens of five early-flowering grasses to help investigate sensitisation or allergy. The result should be related to symptoms: a positive result without symptoms may be sensitisation only, while a negative result does not completely rule out allergy.
desc.k17342: The tx9 mix examines specific IgE to the pollens of five tree species to help identify sensitisation or allergy. A positive result should be compared with symptoms, because sensitisation alone does not prove clinical allergy; equally, a negative result does not completely rule it out.
desc.k82260: This profile measures urinary metabolites of several environmental pollutants to assess recent exposure. It includes mycotoxins, toxic metals and chemicals from pesticides, plastics and cosmetics; interpretation takes into account exposure history and the clinical picture.
desc.k18208: The lipid profile measures total cholesterol, HDL, LDL and triglycerides, together with calculated risk indicators. It is used for routine lipid checks and to assess the risk of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease linked to abnormal levels of fats in the blood.
desc.k82250: MycoTox measures 11 mycotoxins in urine to assess exposure to toxins produced by moulds in food or damp environments. The laboratory presents it as a supporting test when exposure is suspected and there are unexplained complaints; interpretation requires the clinical history and possible sources of exposure.
desc.k82257: TOXDetect measures 27 metabolites of organophosphate pesticides, phthalates, bisphenols and parabens in urine to assess recent exposure. It does not identify the exact source, and the presence of metabolites does not necessarily mean disease; interpretation requires exposure history and clinical information.
desc.k17927: Progesterone is measured to assess ovulation, causes of infertility and abnormal uterine bleeding. It is also used in some high-risk pregnancies and to monitor progesterone treatment, taking into account the phase of the cycle or stage of pregnancy.
desc.k17486: Procalcitonin is used as a supporting marker in assessing sepsis and systemic infections, especially when the clinical picture is unclear. It helps distinguish bacterial from non-bacterial infections and monitor the course of the illness and the response to antimicrobial treatment.
desc.k17929: Prolactin is assessed in menstrual cycle and ovulation disorders, galactorrhoea, infertility or male reproductive disorders. The measurement helps investigate hyperprolactinaemia and follow up prolactinoma; the level varies during the day, and a rise during pregnancy or breastfeeding is interpreted in that context.
desc.k17700: Protein C helps limit blood clotting. The test looks for protein C deficiency when assessing a tendency to thrombosis and is usually combined with other thrombophilia markers, especially in people who have had a thrombosis and their relatives.
desc.k17714: Protein S supports the anticoagulant action of protein C. Measuring the free antigen is used to look for its deficiency when investigating a tendency to thrombosis, usually with other thrombophilia markers, in patients with thrombosis and their relatives.
desc.k17502: Measures the total amount of protein lost in the urine over 24 hours to assess proteinuria and kidney damage. It helps investigate kidney disease or systemic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension and lupus; in pregnancy, a rise may be linked to pre-eclampsia.
desc.k17420: Total protein shows the overall amount of protein in the blood, mainly albumin and globulins. The test is used in routine check-ups and in assessing liver and kidney disease, metabolic disorders, malabsorption or malnutrition, including nutritional follow-up and preparation before surgery.
desc.k17930: PTH reflects the secretory activity of the parathyroid glands and helps determine whether high or low calcium is related to their function. It is assessed in hyperparathyroidism and disorders of calcium metabolism; measurement during surgery can help assess whether an adenoma has been removed.
desc.k17950: Renin is part of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system, which regulates blood pressure and the balance of water and electrolytes. The measurement, often together with aldosterone, is used to investigate secondary hypertension, adrenal disorders and the response to treatment for blood pressure or electrolyte disorders.
desc.k17696: Counts reticulocytes, immature red blood cells that reflect the production activity of the bone marrow. It helps clarify anaemia and follow the response after treatment with iron, B12 or folate, chemotherapy or transplantation, and is interpreted together with the full blood count.
desc.k17738: Rheumatoid factor is a group of autoantibodies against IgG and is used as an aid in the diagnosis, prognosis and follow-up of rheumatoid arthritis. It is usually assessed together with CRP and anti-CCP; its presence is not specific, as it can also be seen in other diseases.
desc.k20368: The ROMA index combines CA 125, HE4 and menopausal status to calculate the likelihood of epithelial ovarian malignancy in women with a pelvic mass that has not yet been diagnosed. The result supports clinical assessment and should be considered alongside other examinations.
desc.k29210: This rapid test detects SARS-CoV-2 antigen in the respiratory mucosa and gives a qualitative positive or negative result. It is used to assess the presence of the virus; the doctor may request an additional PCR depending on symptoms and the clinical situation.
desc.k29740: Quantitatively measures IgG against the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein to document the antibody response after infection or vaccination. The test gives the antibody concentration and is not used to diagnose acute COVID-19; the result is reviewed according to the timing of exposure or immunisation.
desc.k22539: This serological test measures IgM antibodies to SARS-CoV-2, whose presence may be linked to a recent infection. According to the description, the result serves as supporting information and does not give a definitive diagnosis of acute infection, which requires medical assessment.
desc.k17695: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is an indirect marker of inflammation. It is used as an aid to detect and monitor inflammatory processes in infections, tumours or autoimmune diseases, including temporal arteritis, systemic vasculitis, polymyalgia rheumatica and rheumatoid arthritis.
desc.k18067: Examines prostate secretion for bacteria and fungi when there are urinary symptoms, recurrent infections or perineal and pelvic pain. When clinically significant bacteria are found, antibiotic susceptibility testing is carried out to support the choice of treatment.
desc.k17996: Detects and quantifies Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma in prostatic secretion, with the option of antibiotic susceptibility testing. It is used for urinary symptoms, pelvic pain or pain after ejaculation, and in the assessment of infertility when an infectious cause is suspected.
desc.k18070: This examination classifies vaginal discharge into groups according to its appearance and the microorganisms described. It is used to help assess increased discharge, itching, burning or genital discomfort and to guide the doctor in investigating the flora and infections.
desc.k18241: Selenium is an essential trace element for antioxidant enzymes and other metabolic functions. Measuring it in the blood helps assess nutritional status and identify deficiency or excess, especially in malabsorption, inadequate nutrition or use of supplements, which can lead to toxicity.
desc.k17951: Measures serotonin in blood or urine, a molecule with nervous, gastrointestinal and vascular roles. The description links the measurement to neuroendocrine assessment and serotonin-secreting tumours; interpretation requires care regarding the effects of diet, medicines and the clinical condition.
desc.k18002: A semen analysis examines the physical characteristics of semen and its microscopic elements, including the number, motility, vitality and shape of sperm cells. The analysis gives a laboratory assessment of the sample; the source stresses that a single sample is not enough to characterise semen quality.
desc.k18146: Anaerobic semen culture looks for bacteria that can cause infection of the prostate, seminal tract or testicles. It is used when there is testicular/pelvic pain, blood in the semen or difficult and painful urination; isolated pathogens can be tested for antibiotic susceptibility.
desc.k18003: Semen culture aims to isolate bacteria and fungi that may be linked to infection of the prostate, seminal tract or testicles. It is requested when there is pain, blood in the semen or urinary symptoms; significant growth of pathogens may be followed by an antibiogram.
desc.k17981: Sputum culture looks for bacteria or fungi that can cause infection of the bronchi and lungs. It is used for thick secretions, difficulty breathing or chest pain; microscopy helps assess sample quality, and isolated pathogens may be accompanied by an antibiogram.
desc.k36707: PCR looks for Neisseria gonorrhoeae DNA in a genital or urine sample, as an aid to identifying the pathogen in the context of sexually transmitted infections. The description highlights detection of genetic material even at low concentrations and the option of using several sample types.
desc.k36708: PCR looks for Ureaplasma urealyticum DNA in genital material or urine, to help detect this pathogen in the context of sexually transmitted infections. The description highlights the method's ability to identify even low concentrations of the microorganism.
desc.k36709: This panel uses PCR to identify two sexually transmitted pathogens chosen from the laboratory's list. Looking for their DNA in a genital or urine sample helps investigate the causes of symptoms in the genital tract.
desc.k36710: This panel uses PCR to look for the DNA of three sexually transmitted pathogens chosen from the laboratory's menu. Testing the genital or urine sample helps identify the causes of genital tract symptoms, according to the selection requested.
desc.k36711: Uses PCR to look for the DNA of four pathogens chosen from the laboratory's list for sexually transmitted infections. The panel is tailored to the pathogens requested and helps investigate genital tract symptoms using a swab, urine or semen.
desc.k36712: Looks for the genetic material of five selected pathogens that cause sexually transmitted infections. The selection is made from the laboratory's list, which includes Ureaplasma, Mycoplasma, Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Treponema pallidum and Trichomonas vaginalis, to investigate genital tract infections.
desc.k36718: This PCR panel looks for the genetic material of six sexually transmitted pathogens chosen from the laboratory's list. It aims to identify the causes of genital symptoms; the options include Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Ureaplasma, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Treponema pallidum and Trichomonas vaginalis.
desc.k36714: The single STD1 test looks for Mycoplasma genitalium DNA by PCR. It is part of the laboratory diagnosis of sexually transmitted pathogens that can cause genital tract symptoms; the source describes several sample types depending on sex.
desc.k36715: This test looks for Mycoplasma hominis DNA by PCR in urogenital samples. The description places it within the diagnosis of sexually transmitted infections and genital complaints, with the option of using a swab, urine or seminal fluid as appropriate.
desc.k36717: This test looks for Treponema pallidum DNA by PCR as part of the diagnosis of sexually transmitted infections.
desc.k36716: This test looks for Trichomonas vaginalis DNA in genital material or urine to help identify this pathogen in the context of sexually transmitted infections. The description presents PCR as a method for detecting genetic material even when the amount of the pathogen is low.
desc.k36713: This test looks for Ureaplasma parvum DNA by PCR in urogenital samples. The description places it within the diagnosis of sexually transmitted infections and genital symptoms, using a swab, urine or semen depending on the type of sample chosen.
desc.k36719: A PCR panel that looks for the DNA of the seven genital pathogens named in the test, to help diagnose sexually transmitted infections. It includes Chlamydia, gonococcus, Trichomonas and species of Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma, with samples adapted to sex and the site of infection.
desc.k36720: This panel looks for the DNA of the eight sexually transmitted infection pathogens listed in the test name. The samples described include genital swabs, seminal fluid and first-morning urine.
desc.k17995: Looks for Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS), which can colonise the genital tract without symptoms but be passed to the baby during birth. Screening during pregnancy helps identify carriage and allows the doctor to plan measures to prevent infections in the newborn.
desc.k17931: SHBG is a transport protein for sex hormones and is important for interpreting androgen status. The measurement can help investigate hirsutism, PCOS and disorders of puberty or monitor hormone therapy, and is assessed together with other hormones.
desc.k17932: Measures total triiodothyronine to assess thyroid function, especially when hyperthyroidism is suspected. It is used when TSH is outside the expected range and to follow disorders of hormone production, usually together with TSH and T4 or FT4.
desc.k17933: Measures the hormone thyroxine (T4) to help assess thyroid function and follow disorders of hormone production. It is used when hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism is suspected and is interpreted together with TSH and other markers depending on the clinical situation.
desc.k17690: The direct Coombs test looks for antibodies bound to the surface of red blood cells, which may be associated with their immune destruction. It helps investigate autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and is interpreted together with clinical and laboratory signs of haemolysis.
desc.k17671: This two-sample test measures free cortisol in saliva in the morning and evening, to compare the daily rhythm of secretion. The laboratory offers it as part of a functional assessment of fatigue, sleep and the stress response; results are interpreted according to the history and clinical picture.
desc.k17672: This panel of four salivary cortisol measurements describes the daily change in free cortisol and the rhythm of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis. The laboratory offers it in the functional assessment of fatigue, sleep disorders and stress-related complaints, and it requires interpretation according to the clinical picture.
desc.k64331: Tracks oestradiol and progesterone in 11 saliva samples over the cycle, as well as testosterone at the start of the cycle. It aims to provide information on ovulation, the luteal phase and hormonal balance in irregular cycles, difficulty conceiving or premenstrual symptoms.
desc.k64333: This salivary profile tracks oestradiol and progesterone over the cycle, testosterone on day three, and the daily rhythm of cortisol and melatonin. It aims to provide information on ovulation, the luteal phase and how hormonal balance relates to sleep, stress and fatigue.
desc.k20034: The SIBO test measures hydrogen and methane in exhaled breath after lactulose to assess small intestinal bacterial overgrowth and increased methane production. It helps investigate bloating, wind, diarrhoea or constipation and monitor the response to treatment.
desc.k17936: Measures testosterone to assess testicular function, disorders of puberty, infertility or erectile dysfunction and to monitor hormone treatment. In women it may be requested when there is hirsutism, virilisation, bleeding or irregular cycles and difficulty becoming pregnant.
desc.k17432: Assesses the total capacity of transferrin to bind iron, helping investigate iron deficiency or iron overload. It is interpreted together with iron, ferritin and haemoglobin to distinguish different patterns of anaemia and iron metabolism disorders.
desc.k18189: Measures thyroglobulin, a protein produced by thyroid tissue, mainly for follow-up after treatment of differentiated thyroid cancer. A rise after removal and ablation of the gland may signal residual tissue or recurrence; anti-Tg antibodies can distort the measurement and are assessed alongside it.
desc.k17442: Total bilirubin helps diagnose and monitor liver disease, haemolytic anaemias and jaundice in newborns. The measurement is requested when there are signs of liver damage, bile duct obstruction or liver-related metabolic disorders.
desc.k18185: Measures total PSA to help assess tumour diseases of the prostate, monitor the response to therapy and detect recurrence. The description includes men with urinary symptoms and preventive check-ups over the age of 50; the result should be combined with clinical assessment and other examinations.
desc.k17768: Avidity measures the binding strength of IgG antibodies to Toxoplasma gondii and helps distinguish a recent infection from a past one. It is particularly important during pregnancy and is interpreted together with IgG, IgM and exposure history.
desc.k17767: Detects specific antibodies to Treponema pallidum to help diagnose syphilis and to assess results after other serological tests. Reactivity can persist for years or for life after treatment, so on its own it does not prove active infection; a non-reactive result may not rule out early infection.
desc.k17424: Transferrin is the protein that carries iron in the blood, and changes in it help assess iron metabolism. The test is used when iron deficiency or overload is suspected and in investigating anaemia, together with haemoglobin, ferritin and serum iron.
desc.k17425: Triglycerides are fats that serve as a source and store of energy, and high levels are linked to cardiovascular risk. The measurement is included in the lipid profile for routine check-ups, risk assessment and monitoring the effect of medicines or lifestyle changes.
desc.k17939: Second-trimester prenatal screening that combines AFP, hCG and unconjugated oestriol with ultrasound data. It calculates the likelihood of certain chromosomal abnormalities, including trisomies 21/18, and of neural tube defects; the test assesses risk and is not in itself a diagnosis.
desc.k17800: Tryptase is a marker of mast cell activation. The measurement helps confirm an anaphylactic reaction when the diagnosis is unclear and can be used in assessing or monitoring disorders with increased mast cell numbers or activity.
desc.k17911: Cardiac troponin I appears in the circulation when heart muscle cells are damaged. It is used as an aid in diagnosing acute myocardial infarction (heart attack), assessing prognosis and monitoring treatment or unstable angina; serial measurements help assess how the damage develops.
desc.k17910: Cardiac troponin T passes into the blood when heart muscle cells are damaged. The test helps diagnose acute myocardial infarction (heart attack), assess prognosis and monitor the course of the condition or unstable angina; serial measurements at clinical intervals help interpret changes.
desc.k17935: Measures TSH, the hormone that regulates thyroid hormone production. It is used together with T3/T4 or the free fractions to diagnose and monitor hypo- and hyperthyroidism, for an enlarged thyroid or thyroid nodules, and in certain checks during pregnancy and in newborns.
desc.k17477: Measures coenzyme Q10, which is important for mitochondrial energy production and antioxidant protection. According to the description, it is used to assess deficiency, levels during statin use or suspected mitochondrial dysfunction, as well as in certain heart conditions selected by the doctor.
desc.k17492: UIBC assesses the unsaturated (free) iron-binding capacity and is used as an indirect marker of transferrin. Together with TIBC, haemoglobin, iron and ferritin, it helps investigate anaemia or iron overload and iron metabolism.
desc.k17426: Urea is a breakdown product of proteins that is formed in the liver and removed by the kidneys. The measurement helps assess kidney function, investigate signs of kidney disease and monitor its course or the effect of treatment.
desc.k18121: This urine culture detects, identifies and quantifies Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma urealyticum/parvum. It is used in investigating urogenital symptoms and fertility problems; according to the description, the test also includes susceptibility testing to certain antibiotics.
desc.k17976: Urine culture identifies and counts microorganisms that can cause urinary tract infection. It is requested for frequent urination, burning, flank pain, fever or other signs; significant growth of pathogens is followed by an antibiogram to help choose treatment.
desc.k18016: Fungal urine culture looks for the growth of fungi, mainly Candida, to help assess candiduria. The result is related to symptoms and to factors such as a urinary catheter, antibiotics, diabetes or immunosuppression, because colonisation and contamination can give positive findings.
desc.k17989: VDRL detects non-specific antibodies that may form during syphilis and is used for screening and for monitoring the response to treatment. A reactive result needs assessment with specific tests for Treponema pallidum, because early infection can give a negative result and other conditions can give a false positive.
desc.k18312: Non-invasive prenatal screening of cell-free fetal DNA in the mother's blood, extending the Plus package with a number of defined microdeletions. It gives the risk for the conditions covered and the fetal fraction; a high-risk result requires prenatal diagnostic confirmation.
desc.k18310: VERAcity Core analyses cell-free fetal DNA in the mother's blood to screen for trisomies 21, 18 and 13 and to provide information on the presence of the Y chromosome. The report gives the risk and the fetal fraction; high-risk results must be confirmed by diagnostic testing.
desc.k18311: VERAcity Plus extends the prenatal screening of the Core package with sex chromosome aneuploidies. Analysis of cell-free fetal DNA in the mother's blood reports the risk and the fetal fraction; a high-risk finding requires confirmation with a prenatal diagnostic method.
desc.k18313: Non-invasive prenatal screening that analyses DNA for the risk of aneuploidies, seven microdeletion syndromes and 100 monogenic diseases. It uses the mother's blood and a cheek swab from the biological father; a high-risk result should be confirmed with a prenatal diagnostic method.
desc.k72588: This test looks for tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) in the removed tick, to assess possible exposure. The result is interpreted by the doctor.
desc.k87378: Measures vitamins K1 and K2 when vitamin K deficiency is suspected; vitamin K is needed to activate clotting factors. Testing may be requested for bleeding or bruising and when diet, fat absorption or certain medicines may reduce the supply of this vitamin.
desc.k17450: Measures retinol to assess vitamin A deficiency or excess. It is used when there are signs such as poor night vision or dry eyes, and when there is a risk from inadequate nutrition; the vitamin is linked to vision, skin, mucous membranes and immune function.
desc.k17451: Measures thiamine, vitamin B1, to assess a deficiency that can affect the nervous system and the heart. The description mentions risk from inadequate nutrition, malabsorption, urinary losses, alcohol or certain medicines, and severe deficiency in beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
desc.k17428: Vitamin B12 is assessed when investigating macrocytic anaemia and neuropathy, when reviewing nutritional status and when monitoring treatment of its deficiency. It plays a role in blood cell formation and DNA synthesis; the description recommends measuring it at the same time as folate.
desc.k17452: Measures vitamin B2, or riboflavin, which takes part in energy production and metabolism through the coenzymes FMN and FAD. The test helps assess deficiency due to inadequate diet, impaired absorption or utilisation, increased elimination and excessive alcohol consumption.
desc.k17453: Vitamin B6 supports metabolism, nerve function and immunity. The measurement helps assess deficiency, which can be associated with anaemia, skin changes or neurological symptoms, especially in kidney disease, malabsorption, inflammatory diseases and excessive alcohol use.
desc.k17475: Measures vitamin C to assess suspected deficiency, which can affect collagen formation, wound healing and the integrity of blood vessels. Testing may help when there is nutritional risk, malabsorption or signs of scurvy.
desc.k17522: The total vitamin D test mainly assesses 25-OH vitamin D to look at its stores, deficiency or excess. It is used in assessing bone disease and calcium and phosphate disorders, and in monitoring the response to supplementation.
desc.k17472: Vitamin E measurement helps confirm deficiency in people with neurological signs, muscle weakness, vision problems or impaired fat absorption. The vitamin is a fat-soluble antioxidant and is assessed together with symptoms and conditions that increase the risk of deficiency.
desc.k17473: Measures biotin, a vitamin needed for the metabolism of proteins, carbohydrates and fats. Testing may help when deficiency is suspected due to inadequate diet, malabsorption, chronic alcohol use, certain medicines or inherited biotinidase deficiency.
desc.k17485: Vitamin K1 is important for forming clotting proteins and for bone metabolism. The blood test is used to check for vitamin K deficiency, especially when there is easy bruising or prolonged bleeding after an injury or procedure.
desc.k18238: Zinc is an essential element for many enzymes and for wound healing. The test helps assess deficiency and monitor treatment, including in people on long-term parenteral nutrition or with digestive diseases, cirrhosis, malignant disease or burns.
desc.k18239: Measures zinc excreted in 24-hour urine, especially when deficiency or increased loss is suspected. The result is assessed alongside serum zinc to distinguish low intake, absorption disorders and urinary or other losses.
desc.k76911: Zonulin Family Peptide is an add-on stool test, offered only together with GI Effects, for zonulin-like peptides. The laboratory presents it as a functional assessment of the intestinal barrier in chronic digestive complaints and for monitoring changes during clinical interventions.

text.Disa ditë para dhe gjatë mbledhjes shman: For a few days before and during collection, avoid alcohol, cigarettes, nuts, tropical fruit, citrus fruit and products containing caffeine, cocoa or vanilla. Avoid physical/mental stress before and during collection.
text.Disa ditë para testimit rekomandohet të: For a few days before testing, it is recommended not to start an elimination diet of the foods included in the panel.
text.Disponueshmëria duhet kontrolluar parapr: Availability must be checked in advance. The laboratory does not take swabs from pregnant women but accepts samples taken by a gynaecologist. text.Dita e ciklit ose faza e shtatzënisë për: The cycle day or stage of pregnancy is decided with the doctor. No special preparation is required; preferably, blood should not be taken immediately after a meal.
text.Dorëzohet guri i plotë. Shpëlahet me ujë: Hand in the whole stone. Rinse it with cold water and dry it for 24 hours at room temperature; keep it in a clean urine container, without liquid, gauze, paper, wrapping or adhesive tape. To collect it, urinate through dense sterile gauze, preferably folded; the first morning urine is important. Do not use gauze washed with detergent. Check carefully for small grains as well. Dry the filtered stone on the gauze for 24 hours; collection can be repeated over several days. Transport dried stones in a urine container kept at room temperature.
Faeces in a kit with transport medium.
text.Feçe në kompletin përkatës, mundësisht j: Faeces in the appropriate kit, preferably the first bowel movement of the morning, without urine or toilet water. With the doctor's approval, stop PPIs, antibiotics and bismuth 14 days before. As instructed and unless the doctor says otherwise, suspend aspirin/NSAIDs, suppositories, enemas, activated charcoal, bismuth, betaine HCl, digestive enzymes, antacids, laxatives, mineral/castor oil and bentonite 2 days before.
text.Feçe të freskëta jo të formuara, rreth n: Fresh unformed faeces, about one teaspoonful in a stool container, without urine/toilet water; at any time, as early as possible after symptoms appear. Deliver as soon as possible; if storage is needed, 2–8°C for up to 2 days or −20°C for longer.
text.Feçe, e njëjta mostër si GI Effects: Faeces, the same sample as GI Effects

text.Feçe, zakonisht nga e njëjta mostër e GI: Faeces, usually from the same GI Effects sample.

text.Feçe; tampon rektal nëse feçet nuk mund: Faeces; rectal swab if faeces cannot be obtained
text.Flokët lahen me shampo të zakonshme neut: Wash the hair with an ordinary neutral shampoo, without zinc, selenium or medicinal ingredients. Do not use conditioner, masks, oils, sprays or anti-dandruff shampoo. The sample must be clean and completely dry. Dyed/chemically treated hair is not accepted; after treatment, wait for 8–12 weeks of regrowth.
text.Genitalet e jashtme lahen me ujë të ngro: Wash the external genitals with warm water and soap. The day before, avoid unprotected intercourse and local vaginal treatment. The sample is not taken during menstruation. The swab is taken using a sterile speculum; check availability in advance. The laboratory does not take swabs from pregnant women but accepts samples taken by a gynaecologist.
text.Genitalet lahen me sapun e shpëlahen mir: Wash the genitals with soap and rinse well, without drying with a towel: women from top to bottom, men from the urethral opening outwards. Collect 10–20 mL from the first stream of the first morning urine; alternatively, do not urinate for 1–2 hours beforehand. Close the sterile container and deliver it promptly. The source excludes collection while taking antibiotics.

text.Gjak i plotë. Rekomandohet pa suplemente: Whole blood. It is recommended to take no mineral supplements for ≥5 days and to avoid possible exposure to metals before the test. The appointment and any therapy/supplements are discussed with the staff.
text.Gjak i plotë; analizohen veçmas eritroci: Whole blood; the erythrocytes are analysed separately.
text.Gjak i shtatzënës dhe të dhëna nga ekogr: Blood from the pregnant woman and ultrasound data.
text.Gjak kapilar, urina e parë e mëngjesit d: Capillary blood, first morning urine and buccal swab
text.Gjak në javët 15–20. Ekografia bëhet par: Blood in weeks 15–20. The ultrasound scan is done before the tests, preferably on the same day; tests within 48 hours after it are accepted. A photocopy of the ultrasound report is needed. No special preparation; preferably not immediately after eating, and no appointment is needed.
text.Gjak në mëngjes esëll, pas 10–12 orësh p: Blood in the morning on an empty stomach, after 10–12 hours without food.
text.Gjak venoz (plazmë, serum, eritrocite os: Venous blood (plasma, serum, erythrocytes or whole blood depending on the parameter) and first morning urine.
text.Gjak venoz dhe urinë 24-orëshe, sipas pë: Venous blood and 24-hour urine, as described
text.Gjak venoz i shtatzënës: Venous blood from the pregnant woman
text.Gjak venoz i shtatzënës dhe tampon bukal: Venous blood from the pregnant woman and a buccal swab from the biological father at the agreed location. An informed consent form is completed.
Venous blood from the pregnant woman and a buccal swab from the biological father.
text.Gjak venoz në mëngjes pas 10–12 orësh pa: Venous blood in the morning after 10–12 hours without food.
text.Gjak venoz pa përgatitje të veçantë. Për: Venous blood, no special preparation. Prepare your family history details and complete the genetic testing informed consent form.

text.Gjak venoz pas 12–14 orësh pa ushqim; sh: Venous blood after 12–14 hours without food; avoid alcohol and vitamin supplements for 24 hours before the sample is taken.
text.Gjak venoz pas rreth 10–12 orësh pa ushq: Venous blood after about 10–12 hours without food or drink other than water. The timing is set according to the purpose of the test and the doctor, as secretion varies during the day.
text.Gjak venoz periferik ose nga kordoni i t: Peripheral venous blood or blood from the newborn's umbilical cord.
text.Gjak venoz periferik ose nga kordoni te: Peripheral venous blood or umbilical cord blood in newborns; no special preparation.
text.Gjak venoz zakonisht në mëngjes, pas 8–1: Venous blood, usually in the morning after 8–10 hours without food; other times as advised by the doctor.
text.Gjak venoz, pa përgatitje të veçantë, pr: Venous blood, no special preparation; preferably not immediately after eating. No appointment needed.
text.Gjak venoz, vetëm në mëngjes pas agjërim: Venous blood, only in the morning after an overnight fast.
text.Gjak venoz, zakonisht në mëngjes pas agj: Venous blood, usually in the morning after an overnight fast.
text.Gjak venoz. Gjatë terapisë tiroide ndiqe: Venous blood. During thyroid therapy, follow the doctor's schedule; the sample is usually taken before the next dose. Without therapy, no special preparation is required, but avoid having the sample taken immediately after eating.
text.Gjak venoz. Shmanget ejakulimi për 24 or: Venous blood. Avoid ejaculation for 24 hours; prostate examination, biopsy and cystoscopy are done after the blood sample is taken to avoid a falsely raised PSA.
text.Gjak venoz. Zakonisht pa përgatitje të v: Venous blood. Usually no special preparation; the doctor may request 10–12 hours without food. Avoid intense physical activity immediately before the test.
text.Gjak venoz; nuk kërkohet përgatitje e ve: Venous blood; no special preparation is required. Preferably, the sample should not be taken immediately after eating.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë, pr: Venous blood; no special preparation, preferably not immediately after eating.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë, pë: Venous blood; no special preparation, apart from the doctor's individual instructions based on the clinical condition.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë. Nj: Venous blood; no special preparation. Inform the laboratory of any therapy or supplements being taken.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë. Në: Venous blood; no special preparation. For the Double test, it is taken between weeks 11–14 of pregnancy.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë. Or: Venous blood; no special preparation. The time matters because DHEA varies during the day.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë. Si: Venous blood; no special preparation. On the doctor's advice, supplements or foods rich in copper may be avoided; report any medicines and health conditions.
text.Gjak venoz; pa përgatitje të veçantë. në: Venous blood; no special preparation. In pregnancy, weeks 7–10 are suggested as part of TORCH testing.
text.Gjak venoz; për kortizolin e mëngjesit k: Venous blood; for morning cortisol, 20–30 minutes of rest are required before the sample is taken. The time of sampling must be known for interpretation.
text.Gjak venoz; përmendet gjaku i plotë: Venous blood; whole blood is mentioned
text.Gjak venoz; teksti diskuton gjithashtu a: Venous blood; the text also discusses urine testing in general.
text.Gjak venoz; teksti i referohet matjes në: Venous blood; the text refers to measurement in plasma
text.Gjak, i përmendur në përshkrim; fraksion: Blood, mentioned in the description; the fraction is not specified.
text.Gjaku jepet në mëngjes, esëll, pas natës: Blood is given in the morning on an empty stomach, after a night without food. Consult the doctor on whether allergy-causing medicines, antihistamines, oral corticosteroids or H2 blockers should be suspended 24 hours before the blood sample is taken.
text.Gjaku merret 4 orë pas dozës së fundit t: Blood is taken 4 hours after the last dose of low-molecular-weight heparin or 6 hours after the last dose of unfractionated heparin.
text.Gjaku merret në mëngjes esëll. Rekomando: Blood is taken in the morning on an empty stomach. At least 30 minutes lying down before the sample, rest and avoiding stress are recommended. text.Gjaku merret në mëngjes, esëll, pas 10–1: Blood is taken in the morning on an empty stomach, after 10–12 hours overnight without food.

text.Hidhet urina e parë e mëngjesit dhe shën: Discard the first morning urine and note the time; collect every urination during the day/night, including the following morning's urine. text.Komplet i posaçëm; feçe spontane, ideali: Special kit; spontaneous stool, ideally from the morning, without urine/toilet water and not during haemorrhoidal/menstrual bleeding. text.Komplet i posaçëm; feçe spontane, mundës: Special kit; spontaneous stool, preferably from the morning, without urine/toilet water. Usually one sample; when three are required, collect them Friday–Saturday–Sunday and hand them in together on Sunday/Monday, within 3–5 days from the first to the last. Wait ≥4 weeks after a colonoscopy/barium; ≥14 days after antibiotics, antiparasitics, antifungals/probiotics, ideally 28 after antibiotics. With the doctor: no PPIs/antibiotics/bismuth for 14 days if H. pylori is added; 2 days without aspirin/NSAIDs, suppositories, enemas, activated charcoal, bismuth, betaine HCl, digestive enzymes, antacids, laxatives, mineral/castor oil/bentonite. Follow the instructions.
text.Komplet i posaçëm; preferohet feçja e më: Special kit; a morning stool is preferred, without urine/toilet water. After a colonoscopy/barium enema, wait ≥4 weeks. After antibiotics, antiparasitics, antifungals/probiotics: ≥14 days, ideally 28 after antibiotics. With H. pylori: PPIs, antibiotics/bismuth are suspended for 14 days only with medical approval. Follow the kit instructions.
text.Komplet i posaçëm; zakonisht në mëngjes: Special kit; usually in the morning after 8–12 hours without food. Avoid B vitamins, especially folate/B6/B12, for 3 days and alcohol for at least 24 hours, unless medically instructed otherwise. Continue your usual therapy unless the doctor advises otherwise; there are no other dietary restrictions, and testing is not recommended during an acute infection. Read the kit instructions.
text.Komplet për feçe, mundësisht jashtëqitja: Stool kit, preferably the first bowel movement, without contamination with urine/water. Abroad: Monday until 10:00. Wait ≥4 weeks after a colonoscopy/barium; ≥14 days after antibiotics, antiparasitics, antifungals/probiotics, ideally 28 after antibiotics. If H. pylori is included: with the doctor's approval, no PPIs, antibiotics/bismuth for 14 days. For 2 days, unless the doctor instructs otherwise: pause aspirin/NSAIDs, suppositories, enemas, activated charcoal, bismuth, betaine HCl, digestive enzymes, antacids, laxatives, mineral/castor oil and bentonite. Follow the GI Effects instructions.
text.Komplet shtëpiak me 11 mostra në ditët e: Home kit with 11 samples on set days, usually starting on day 3; label and freeze immediately. Deliver frozen as soon as possible, ideally the morning after the last sample; accepted every day. For 30 minutes before: no food, drinks other than water, tooth brushing or chewing gum. The evening before, avoid alcohol, intense activity and stress. Do not change medicines/supplements without consultation. Avoid a cycle with planned procedures, travel or stress; read the instructions.
text.Komplet shtëpiak me mostra në orare të c: Home kit with samples at set times, dried on filter paper for 24 hours at room temperature; if not delivered within 48 hours, freeze them. No alcohol/intense exercise for 24 hours; no creatine, bananas/legumes for 48 hours. Supplements as instructed; therapy is changed only with the doctor. Cycle day as per the kit; men and women without a cycle/postmenopausal on any day.
text.Komplet shtëpiak, protokoll 2/3-orësh; n: Home kit, 2/3-hour protocol; at the laboratory, book ≥2 days in advance. As advised by the doctor: 4 weeks without antibiotics/colonoscopy/barium; 2–4 weeks without antimicrobials, antifungals/Pepto-Bismol; 7 days without laxatives, prokinetics, stool softeners/fibre (2–4 in severe constipation). For 24 hours: boiled white meat, eggs, white rice, soup without vegetables, fats, water, weak coffee/tea without additives. For 12 hours, water only. On the day of the test: no toothpaste, chewing gum, sweets, mouthwash, smoking/exercise; no sleeping 1 hour before/during; avoid non-essential preparations. Not during an acute intestinal infection.
text.Komplet shtëpiak: 07:00–09:00 dhe 23:30–: Home kit: 07:00–09:00 and 23:30–00:30, about 2 mL in each tube. Reduce foam by tapping gently; close/freeze the samples immediately and keep them frozen until delivery. For 30 minutes beforehand: no food/drinks other than water, smoking, chewing gum, sweets, tooth brushing, mouthwash or lip cosmetics. Rinse the mouth with cold water 10 minutes before. The saliva should be clear, without mucus; avoid coughing, intense exertion and stress. Insufficient samples are not analysed.
text.Kompleti GI Effects; preferohet feçja e: GI Effects kit; a morning stool is preferred, but any spontaneous sample is accepted, without urine/toilet water. Waiting times: ≥4 weeks after a colonoscopy/barium enema; ≥14 days after antibiotics, antiparasitics, antifungals/probiotics, ideally 28 days after antibiotics. Read the instructions.
text.Kompleti shtëpiak: 07:00–09:00, 11:00–13: Home kit: 07:00–09:00, 11:00–13:00, 15:00–17:00, 22:00–00:00; DHEA from the first sample. Close and label the tubes, place them in the bag and freeze immediately; deliver frozen, preferably the morning after the night sample.

text.Marrje në çdo orë, nga profesionist përm: Taken at any time by a professional using a sterile speculum. The day before: no sexual intercourse/local vaginal treatment. text.Mblidhen rreth 2 mL në secilën epruvetë: Collect about 2 mL in each tube at 07:00–09:00, 11:00–12:00, 16:00–20:00 and 23:00–00:30; reduce foam by tapping gently. text.Me kompletin shtëpiak mblidhen tri mostr: Three samples are collected with the home kit: 07:00–09:00, 15:00–17:00 and 02:30–03:30. Close, label, bag and freeze each tube immediately; transport them frozen as soon as possible, ideally the morning after the night sample. At night, avoid bright light; dim red light is recommended. text.Me lugën e enës fekale merret sasi sa nj: Using the stool container's spoon, take a hazelnut-sized amount from several areas, especially mucous/liquid parts. Avoid contact with urine/toilet water. Deliver promptly; until then, keep it in the fridge for no more than 2 hours. text.Merren 16 mostra pështyme në ditët/orare: Take 16 saliva samples on the days/at the times set by the kit, usually starting on the third day of the cycle; label, close, bag and freeze each one immediately. text.Merret feçe e lëngshme ose që merr formë: Collect liquid stool or stool that takes the shape of the container, within the first 3 days of symptoms; 2 samples within 24 hours are preferred. text.Merret gjurmë nga zona perianale me shir: An impression is taken from the perianal area with transparent adhesive tape.
text.Merret mostër e freskët sa një lajthi në: Take a fresh hazelnut-sized sample in a stool container, at any time, and send it as soon as possible. The alternative rectal swab is taken by professional staff. For asymptomatic carriage, three samples on three consecutive days are required.
text.Merret nga gjinekologu me instrumente të: Taken by the gynaecologist with special instruments through the cervix, under aseptic conditions. For a few days beforehand, avoid pessaries, creams or vaginal douching, unless the doctor instructs otherwise.
text.Merret nga mjeku gjatë ekzaminimit gjine: Taken by the doctor during a gynaecological examination with instruments through the cervix, under aseptic conditions. For a few days before the sample, avoid vaginal pessaries, creams and douches, unless the doctor instructs otherwise.
text.Merret nga mjeku/personeli i trajnuar në: Taken by the doctor/trained staff at any time, at least 12 hours after antiseptic use; the material is taken from the lesion with a sterile swab. For lesions with pus, staff collect the material after spontaneous drainage or sterile opening, with local cleaning and sterile instruments.
text.Merret nga personel i trajnuar me tampon: Taken by trained staff with a sterile swab from several deep areas, avoiding bleeding and foreign bodies. Can be taken during the day, preferably before the dressing is changed.
text.Merret nga profesionisti me tampon steri: Taken by a professional with a thin sterile swab, about 2 cm inside the urethra. Before the first morning urination or at least 2 hours after urinating during the day; a sample taken by a urologist and delivered by the patient/doctor's practice is also accepted.
text.Merret nga urologu pas higjienës dhe mas: Taken by the urologist after hygiene and prostatic massage, on a swab/in a sterile container, with urine before/after according to the 2- or 4-glass test. The 4-glass test includes 5–8 mL of initial stream, midstream, secretion and 2–3 mL after massage; the 2-glass test describes midstream, secretion and 2–3 mL after massage. Transport within ≤2 hours at room temperature. No urination for ≥2 hours, no ejaculation for 2 days, no genital creams for 1 day. Contraindicated in acute prostatitis; midstream first morning urine is recommended.
text.Merret një mostër e rastësishme feçesh d: A random stool sample is taken and stored at 2–8°C until delivery to the laboratory.
text.Merret para antibiotikëve dhe të paktën: Taken before antibiotics and at least 12 hours after a local antiseptic or rinsing with saline solution.
